lines: appinfo/info.xml states no <repository>.

<repository> is the only machine-readable link from a published release back to the source it was built from, and <bugs> is where the App Store page sends a report. Without them a user of the release has no way back to the project.
Declares Nextcloud 26 to 28; the oldest maintained major is 32 (as of 2026-09), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
max-version 28 is below the oldest maintained major (32, as of 2026-09), so the release covers only servers that no longer receive fixes.
min-version 26 reaches below the oldest maintained major (32), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
engines.node ^16.0.0 in package.json admits only end-of-life Node lines: the release is built on Node 16, which reached end of life on 2023-09-11.
That Node receives no security fixes, and the lockfile is resolved for it. The oldest line still maintained is Node 22.
Node release dates from schedule.json in nodejs/Release, as of 2026-10-22.
package.json without a lockfile.
Every install resolves the ranges afresh, so two builds of the same commit can contain different code, and npm ci - what CI uses - does not run at all.
package.json scripts stylelint, stylelint:fix call stylelint, and no Stylelint configuration is in the checkout.
stylelint css/*.css css/*.scss src/**/*.scss src/**/*.vue
The command is there to be run, so whoever runs it gets a tool that has nothing to go by - and CI, if it runs the script, reports the failure as the change under test.
Licence agpl (appinfo/info.xml, package.json).
agpl in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as AGPLv3+, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. An SPDX id there needs a <nextcloud> min-version of 31 or higher.
No SPDX id: agpl (package.json). Only an SPDX id says which licence is meant, and for a GNU licence whether -only or -or-later.
No LICENSES/ directory, so the licence text itself is not in the checkout, which is what REUSE and the distributions check for.
The app id is dokuwiki, the checkout directory is nextcloud-app-dokuwiki.

The server finds an app by its directory name, so the installed directory has to be named after the id. A checkout can be named anything, which is why this is a note and not a defect - but a tarball built from this directory name would not load.
PHP floor stated once: appinfo/info.xml min-version 8.1; no composer.json in the checkout.
Nothing contradicts anything here. Stating it in both places is what keeps a composer install from resolving packages for a PHP the server will not run.
appinfo/info.xml caps PHP at max-version 8.3.
A server on a newer PHP refuses to enable the app, so this cap has to be raised deliberately with every PHP release, not left where it was.
Node stated as ^16.0.0 (package.json engines.node).
Not stated in .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.
Tooling in the checkout: ESLint (.eslintrc.js, superseded form).

ESLint is configured in .eslintrc.js: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8.
No Stylelint configuration: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly.
No Psalm configuration: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does.
No PHPUnit configuration: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change.
No PHP-CS-Fixer configuration: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command.
No REUSE configuration: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for.
No EditorConfig configuration: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does.
5 declared packages are named nowhere in the checkout: css-minimizer-webpack-plugin, file-loader, webpack-cli, webpack-merge, webpack-node-externals.

Searched as literal names over 321 files, package.json excluded apart from its non-dependency fields, lockfiles excluded; then as an ESLint shorthand, as what TypeScript takes from a tsconfig, and as a peer of an installed package in package-lock.json. A package loaded some other way is not named anywhere either, so this is a list to check, not a list to remove.
Version 1.0.3 in appinfo/info.xml and package.json.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
make reads GNUmakefile and never Makefile; it runs only with make -f <name>.
Every directory the shipped PHP reaches through __DIR__ and the frontend through linkTo is in the shipped file set (the ncmake core and ncmake.mk).
